content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (ASSIGN), confidence 0.76.**

**What I found.** Section 10.3 ("Assignment", paragraph p0063) is a bare successors-and-assigns binding clause. It contains no consent standard and no transfer restriction on either party. I confirmed by search that the Agreement has no "change of control" language at all, and no other consent or successor provisions bearing on assignment.

**Direction analysis.** Nothing here binds us adversely: there is no blanket prohibition on Company assignment, no M&A gap to fix defensively, and no HDI termination or re-pricing right on our change of control — so this is not walk-away territory, and I did not flag the parts that favour us. The failure is on the vendor side: HDI is free to assign this site-development and hosting engagement — including to a competitor of ours — with no notice and no consent. The fallback requires a consent standard for assignments other than to successors, so the clause misses the fallback on a material term of a high-severity rule.

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level, keyed to precedent seed-assign).** A minimal append to 10.3 that preserves the existing sentence and adds: (i) Company assignment without consent to an affiliate or transaction successor; (ii) no HDI assignment without our prior written consent, not unreasonably withheld, and never to a competitor; (iii) confirmation that our change of control gives HDI no termination, suspension or re-pricing right.

One judgment call worth surfacing: because the current clause is silent rather than restrictive, an alternative reading is that it already exceeds the fallback for us and should be left alone. I flagged it because the unrestricted vendor-side transfer right is a genuine exposure in a hosting relationship, but the edit is drafted so it only adds protection and takes nothing away from our own assignment freedom — an easy clause to drop if the commercial team prefers not to reopen boilerplate.
